title: Validation of research site mentorship as an approach for increasing study site performance (enrollment)

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Validation of research site mentorship as an approach for increasing study site performance (enrollment)》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】The identification of strategies that improve participant enrollment in clinical trials remains a key focus of stakeholders in this field, due to its role as a leading indicator of timely trial completion and its contributions to the validity and generalizability of clinical trial results.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Validation of research site mentorship as an approach for increasing study site performance (enrollment)》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】The "Total Randomized Participants (#) by Mentee Site" and the "Percentage of Randomized Participants (Actual/Expected) Monthly Average By Site (%)" were evaluated across participating mentee study sites over three time periods: 1) 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP), 2) 5-month intervention period (IP), and 3) 3-month follow-up period (FUP).

【Abstract · abstract-1-6】Our findings demonstrate an association between the NODES site mentorship model and improvements in most mentee sites' "Total Randomized Participants (#)" (4/7; 57%) at the end of the 5-month intervention period (IP), as compared to the 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP) (Table B).

evidence.text: The "Total Randomized Participants (#) by Mentee Site" and the "Percentage of Randomized Participants (Actual/Expected) Monthly Average By Site (%)" were evaluated across participating mentee study sites over three time periods: 1) 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP), 2) 5-month intervention period (IP), and 3) 3-month follow-up period (FUP).

Our findings demonstrate an association between the NODES site mentorship model and improvements in most mentee sites' "Total Randomized Participants (#)" (4/7; 57%) at the end of the 5-month intervention period (IP), as compared to the 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP) (Table B).
